title: Kinetic Inspector: Tile-based Compact Dashboard for Per-model & Per-route Metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact, tile-oriented dashboard called 'Kinetic Inspector' for per-model and per-route performance views. Goal: enable engineers and platform owners to quickly scan latency, throughput, token distribution, and cost signals across routes and model variants in a single compact surface. The UI should be dense but legible at 1–2 rows per route, support small multiples, and expose quick drill-ins to the existing detailed route canvas. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma prototype for desktop, chart-specs for four micro-widgets (latency sparkline + distribution baton, throughput minibars, token composition radial, cost delta band), accessibility notes, and a short interaction spec for rollout-aware annotations.
acceptance_criteria: Tile layout renders legibly at 320px and above with provided example dataset (see test_plan).
Latency tile shows p50/p95/p99 markers and an anomaly flag when p95 increases >25% over baseline.
Throughput tile supports live aggregation toggle (requests/s vs tokens/s) and displays a stack for model variants.
Token composition tile breaks out prompt vs completion tokens and highlights cache hits as an inline percentage.
Cost delta band surfaces per-route unit-cost and 24h delta with color-coded thresholds and links to Optimize recommendations.
Prototype includes keyboard navigation for tile focus, tooltips with exact values, and ARIA labels for major elements.
decisions: Use tile microcomponents (MicroSpark, DeltaBand, MiniRing, VariantStack) to maximize reuse across Console canvases.
Default view will be per-route collapsed tiles; user can switch to per-model grouping via top-left toggle.
Latency micro-sparkline uses density-based smoothing by default with explicit p95/P99 overlay; smoothing toggle available in settings.
Integrate rollout state indicator (canary/primary/fallback) as a small badge on the left edge of each tile to reduce context switching.
comments: 2025-02-19 - Tomás Rivera (ENG): Shared a lightweight API contract for the microtiles (latencySeries, throughputSeries, tokenBreakdown, costSummary).
2025-02-22 - Marta Chen (DES): Uploaded initial mid-fi canvases; requested guidance on color thresholds for cost deltas.
2025-02-25 - Priya Singh (PM): Suggest adding explicit cross-region indicator—some customers saw divergent latencies by region.
2025-02-27 - Alex Moreno (ENG): Noted that p99 will be expensive to compute on query; recommended precomputed rollout-friendly histograms.
2025-03-03 - Design review: Iterated on spacing, decreased tile height from 96px to 84px to fit more routes on-page while preserving legibility.
review_feedback: Design Review 2025-03-03 - Leads: Overall strong. Action: document fallback for missing token breakdown (show 'n/a' with help tooltip) and add unit tests for keyboard nav.
Accessibility: Ensure color-blind safe palette for delta bands; provide texture patterns for high/low change states.
PM: Add quick link from each tile to the rollout timeline and to the Evaluate prompt-set that produced the anomaly.
implementation_notes: Microcomponents should expose a compact prop set: {series, baseline, unit, thresholds, onDrillIn}.
Frontend: implement using existing chart primitives in console-lib; prefer canvas-backed sparklines to improve rendering at scale.
Backend: pre-aggregate histogram buckets for latency windows (1s/10s/1m) to support p99 approximations without high CPU cost.
Telemetry: emit tile-impression and tile-drill events with route/model tags for A/B measurement.
test_plan: Load the prototype with latency-example-dataset.csv and verify p95/p99 markers align with expected values.
Simulate 1,000 concurrent tiles to validate rendering performance and keyboard navigation focus order.
Verify cost delta color thresholds at 5%, 15%, and 30% increases and that Optimize recommendations link opens in a new tab.
notes_for_release: Feature gated off by default; enable via console.featureFlags.kineticInspector. Beta rollout to 10% of orgs for 2 weeks, monitor tile-impression and drill rates.
